verses.text: Around that time, a huge crowd had nothing to eat. Jesus called his disciples over and said:
“I feel for these people. They’ve been with me three days and have nothing to eat.
“If I send them home hungry, they’ll collapse on the way. Some came from far away.”
His disciples answered, “Where could anyone get enough bread to feed this crowd out here in the middle of nowhere?”
Jesus asked them, “How many loaves do you have?” They said, “Seven.”
He told the crowd to sit on the ground. Then he took the seven loaves, gave thanks, broke them, and handed them to his disciples to serve. They passed them around to the crowd.
They also had a few small fish. Jesus blessed them and told the disciples to serve those too.
The people ate and were satisfied. The disciples picked up seven baskets of leftover pieces.
About four thousand people had eaten. Then Jesus sent them home.
Right away, he got into the boat with his disciples and came to the region of Dalmanutha.
The Pharisees came out and started questioning him. To test him, they demanded a sign from heaven.
Jesus sighed deeply and said, “Why does this generation keep demanding a sign? I’m telling you the truth: no sign will be given to this generation.”
He left them, got back into the boat, and crossed to the other side.
The disciples had forgotten to bring bread. They had only one loaf in the boat.
Jesus warned them, “Watch out! Beware the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod.”
They started discussing it with each other: “He said that because we didn’t bring bread.”
Jesus knew what they were saying and asked, “Why are you talking about having no bread? Don’t you see or understand yet? Are your hearts still hard?
“You have eyes—can’t you see? You have ears—can’t you hear? Don’t you remember?
“When I broke five loaves for five thousand people, how many baskets of leftovers did you collect?” They answered, “Twelve.”
“And when the seven loaves fed four thousand, how many baskets of leftovers did you collect?” They said, “Seven.”
Jesus asked them, “You still don’t understand?”
They came to Bethsaida. People brought a blind man to Jesus and begged him to touch him.
Jesus took the blind man by the hand and led him outside the village. He spat on the man’s eyes, laid his hands on him, and asked, “Can you see anything?”
The man looked up and said, “I can see people, but they look like walking trees.”
Jesus laid his hands on the man’s eyes again. He looked carefully, his sight was restored, and he could see everything clearly.
Jesus sent him home and said, “Don’t go into the village or tell anyone there.”
Jesus and his disciples went out to the villages around Caesarea Philippi. On the way he asked them, “Who do people say I am?”
They answered, “Some say John the Baptizer; others say Elijah; others say one of the prophets.”
Jesus asked them, “And who do you say I am?” Peter answered, “You are the Christ.”
Jesus strictly warned them not to tell anyone about him.
Then he began teaching them that the Son of Man had to suffer many things, be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and legal teachers, be killed, and rise again after three days.
He spoke openly about this. Peter took him aside and started correcting him.
Jesus turned around, looked at his disciples, and rebuked Peter: “Get behind me, Satan! You’re thinking about human things, not God’s things.”
Jesus called the crowd over with his disciples and said, “If anyone wants to follow me, they must say no to themselves, pick up their cross, and follow me.
“Whoever tries to save their life will lose it. But whoever loses their life for me and for the good news will save it.
“What’s the point of gaining the whole world if you lose your life?
“What could anyone give in exchange for their life?
“Whoever is ashamed of me and my words in this unfaithful, sinful generation—the Son of Man will be ashamed of them too when he comes in his Father’s glory with the holy angels.”
